people.name: 24kGoldn
people.description: American rapper, singer, songwriter 24kGoldn. His single ‘Mood’, featuring Puerto Rican-American rapper Iann Dior, topped the Billboard Hot 100.

people.name: Julia Michaels
people.description: American singer and songwriter Julia Michaels. Her debut solo single in 2017, 'Issues', peaked at No.11 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States. As a songwriter, Michaels has written songs for artists including Selena Gomez, Demi Lovato, Fifth Harmony, Shawn Mendes, Britney Spears, Justin Bieber and Gwen Stefani. She has earned two Billboard Hot 100 No.1 songs with Bieber's 'Sorry' and Gomez's 'Lose You to Love Me'.

people.name: Monique Adrienne Coleman
people.description: Monique Adrienne Coleman, American actress and singer from High School Musical, as part of the cast had the 2006 US No.1 ‘High School Musical’ album and 2007, US No.1 ‘High School Musical 2’ album. Over 17 million viewers in the United States watched the TV premier of High School Musical; making it the highest rated basic cable broadcast in U.S. history.

people.name: Nikolai Fraiture
people.description: Nikolai Fraiture, bassist from American rock band The Strokes who had the 2001 UK No.14 single 'Last Nite' and the 2001 UK No.2 album Is This It.

people.name: Wayne Parker
people.description: Wayne Parker, from the Canadian rock band, Glass Tiger who had the 1986 UK No.29 single 'Don't Forget Me When I'm Gone'. He and his band were honoured with five Canadian Music Industry Juno Awards, multiple Canadian SOCAN Classic Awards and were nominated for a Best New Artist Grammy Award.

people.name: Andrew Ranken
people.description: Andrew Ranken, drummer from Irish-British Celtic punk band The Pogues who scored the 1987 UK No.8 single 'The Irish Rover'.

people.name: Bill Gibson
people.description: Bill Gibson from Huey Lewis and the News who had the 1985 UK No.11 & US No.1 single 'The Power Of Love'. Their third, and best-selling, album was the 1983 Sports, and they contributed to the soundtrack of the 1985 feature film Back to the Future.

people.name: Roger Steen
people.description: Roger Steen, guitar, with American band The Tubes known for their 1977 hit single 'White Punks On Dope' and the 1983 US No.10 single 'She's A Beauty'.

people.name: Terry Reid
people.description: British singer-songwriter Terry Reid. He was a member of Peter Jay's Jaywalkers and opened for The Rolling Stones on their 1966 tour. Reid turned down offers from Jimmy Page to be lead vocalist of the band that became Led Zeppelin and an invite from Ritchie Blackmore to front the newly formed Deep Purple. His fourth album, Seed of Memory, released in 1976, was produced by Graham Nash. Ried later appeared on albums by Don Henley, Jackson Browne and Bonnie Raitt. Reid died of cancer in California on 4 August 2025, aged 75.

people.name: Toy Caldwell
people.description: Toy Caldwell, lead guitarist and main songwriter of the 1970s Southern Rock group The Marshall Tucker Band. He died on 25 February 1993 age 45.

people.name: J.C. Crowley
people.description: American musician J.C. Crowley best known as a member of 1970s soft rock group Player, which scored a US No. 1 hit in 1977 with 'Baby Come Back'.

people.name: John Hammond Jr
people.description: John Hammond Jr, American singer and musician, the son of record producer John H. Hammond. He has worked with many artists including Jimi Hendrix, Eric Clapton, Mike Bloomfield, Dr. John, and Duane Allman.

people.name: Raymond Froggatt
people.description: English songwriter and singer Raymond Froggatt. His band, were initially known as the Buccaneers, later Monopoly and ultimately The Raymond Froggatt Band. The Dave Clark Five had a No. 7 hit in the UK Singles Chart with Froggatt's 'The Red Balloon' in 1968 and his song, 'Big Ship', was a No. 8 UK Singles Chart hit for Cliff Richard in 1969. Froggatt died at Royal Shrewsbury Hospital on 23 July 2023, at the age of 81.

people.name: Timmy Thomas
people.description: American R&B singer, keyboardist, songwriter, and record producer Timmy Thomas best known for his 1972 US No.3 & 1973 UK No.12 single 'Why Can't We Live Together'. In 2015, Drake sampled 'Why Can't We Live Together', on his single 'Hotline Bling'. Thomas died of cancer on 11 March 2022, at the age of 77.

works.title: You Really Got Me
works.eventDescription: American record producer, songwriter, and arranger Shel Talmy died from complications of a stroke at the age of 87. He arranged and produced hits such as 'You Really Got Me' by The Kinks, (and many more hits with the group up to 19670, 'My Generation' by The Who, and 'Friday on My Mind' by the Easybeats. Talmy produced two singles in 1965 by two groups featuring David Bowie, 'I Pity The Fool' by The Manish Boys and 'You've Got A Habit Of Leaving', where the singer was accompanied by The Lower Third.

works.title: The Lion Sleeps Tonight
works.eventDescription: American musician Philip Margo died age 79. He was a long time member of The Tokens, along with his brother Mitch, best known for their hit recording of ‘The Lion Sleeps Tonight’.

works.title: Disco
works.eventDescription: Kylie Minogue went to No.1 on the UK album chart with Disco, making her the only woman to top the chart in five consecutive decades.

works.title: Superstar
works.eventDescription: Leon Russell died in Nashville, he was 74. He led Joe Cocker’s band Mad Dogs & Englishmen and appeared at George Harrison’s 1971 Concert for Bangladesh. Many of his songs became hits for others, among them 'Superstar' (written with Bonnie Bramlett) for the Carpenters, 'Delta Lady' for Joe Cocker and 'This Masquerade' for George Benson. More than 100 acts have recorded 'A Song for You,' which Russell said he wrote in 10 minutes.

works.title: Hello
works.eventDescription: Adele's comeback single 'Hello' achieved platinum sales status in the UK, just three weeks after it was released after the chart-topping song sold more than 600,000 copies.

works.title: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
works.eventDescription: The original collage that was reproduced and included in copies of The Beatles' 1967 classic Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band record sold for $87,720. The piece, which was designed by Peter Blake, was sold to an unnamed bidder as part of an auction of modern British art at Sotheby’s in London.

works.title: Compilation 1
works.eventDescription: The Beatles launched their first official website www.thebeatles.com. The site went live on the same day as the release of their retrospective 'Compilation 1' album.

works.title: Spice
works.eventDescription: A report showed that The Spice Girls were the highest earners in pop during the 90s with their debut album 'Spice' selling over 20 million copies. Elton John was second with 14 million sales from 'The Lion King'.

works.title: The Red Shoes
works.eventDescription: The Kate Bush musical short film The Line, The Cross & The Curve opened at the London Film Festival. The short, starring actress Miranda Richardson as a ballet dancer cursed by magic slippers, is an extended music video featuring songs from Bush's album The Red Shoes.

works.title: Wild Thing
works.eventDescription: Ronnie Bond drummer with The Troggs died. Scored the 1966 US No.1 & UK No.2 single 'Wild Thing' and 1966 UK No.1 ‘With A Girl Like You.’

works.title: Business as Usual
works.eventDescription: Men At Work started a 15-week run at No.1 on the US album chart with their debut album 'Business As Usual', which went on to sell over five million copies in the US.

works.title: Tonight's the Night
works.eventDescription: Rod Stewart started an 8 week run at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'Tonight's The Night'. It was Rod's second US No.1; it made No.5 in the UK after being banned by many radio stations due to song being about the seduction of a virgin. The song features whispers from actress Britt Ekland who was Stewart's girlfriend at the time.

works.title: The Song Remains the Same
works.eventDescription: Led Zeppelin scored their seventh UK No.1 with the film soundtrack double album The Song Remains The Same, peaking at No.2 on the US chart. The tracks were recorded at Madison Square Garden, New York City in 1973.

works.title: Barrett
works.eventDescription: Syd Barrett released his second solo album Barrett only 10 months after his debut The Madcap Laughs. David Gilmour produced the whole album, which also featured performances by Pink Floyd's Richard Wright on keyboards. The album has since been reissued in remastered form with extra tracks from the sessions.

works.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
works.eventDescription: Hugo Montenegro was at No.1 in the UK singles chart with 'The Good The Bad And The Ugly', the soundtrack from a Clint Eastwood spaghetti western film. The first instrumental No.1 since 1963.

works.title: Little Red Rooster
works.eventDescription: Decca Records released The Rolling Stones' 'Little Red Rooster'. Written by Willie Dixon (as The Red Rooster), and previously recorded by Howlin’ Wolf and Sam Cooke, the single was recorded at Chess Studios in Chicago. The single was a No.1 hit in the UK and remains the only time a blues song has ever topped the UK pop chart.
